main_text.l: VI.
Sed quia in corporeo carcere clausus, absq; eius
adminiculis, aut nihil, aut exigua admodum poteft;
omni arte & cura elaborandum eft, ut[?] fui carceris in-
salubritate, perinde ac illi, qui in peftilenti habitat re-
gione, impeditus, aut etiam tabo aliquo contamina-
tus, inualidus ac pene inutilis euadat.
VII.
Quocirca omnes omnium litterarum amantes,
omnium Musarum nomine etiam atq; etiam hor-
tor & oro, ut quàm diligentissime meliori valetudi-
ni comparandæ, atq; conseruandæ incumbant.
IIX.
Etenim mihi videtur Natura de illis iure conqueri
posse, qui cùm ab ea temperatissimum corpus adepti
sunt; illi præclarum adeo ac utile donum, non con-
temnunt modò (cuius etiâ D. Apost. Paulus geri vult
curam) uerùm etiâ corrumpunt, defœdantq;. 1.Thes-
IX.
Vt Galenum noftrum fcribentem, quantumuis
optimas corporis temperaturas otio, alijsq; vitæ &
victus erroribus, mirificè deprauari, verum prodidis-
se conteftentur. In lib. Quod mores animi, &c.
X.
Huic igitur MEDICINA incumbit: tantò ho-
noratior & præftantior, quanto magis Corporis A-
nimiq; robur ac sanitas, aut per se expeti debent, aut
voluptatis & felicitatis gratiâ exoptari.
XI.
Etenim Ars illa est (Ποιητικὴ Factiua) ufu seu Experien-
tia & Ratione constituta ac inuenta, corporis humani
bonam valetudinem custodiendi, perditamq; recu-
peran-

page.notes: Long s was read as plain s throughout (e.g. "claufus" = clausus, "Confil" = Consil). The word after "claufus" is printed "clausus" with an f-shaped long s; the reading is uncertain. The mark before "fui" is a blotted ligature, read as ut[?]. "IIX." is printed as such and left as printed (for VIII). Greek in XI is a clumsy print and only approximated in Greek letters; treat the Greek word as uncertain. The reference line after IX and the line after "defœdantq;" are placed as they appear, below the text, in italic.
